title: Deprecate atoms.get/set_calculator()
body:
Following the relative popularity of #475, this MR takes some steps towards deprecating `atoms.get_calculator()` and `atoms.set_calculator()` since these two methods do neither more nor less than the `atoms.calc` property, and hence are redundant.

Update: Actually after some regex magic and a few dozen manual updates here we are, no more set/get_calculator().  The dangerous part is if there are typos in untested code, but it seems somewhat unlikely.
author: askhl

comments.author: flokno
comments.body: Somewhat related comment: I don't really like `atoms.calc` and would vote for `atoms.calculator` in ase 4.0.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Noted.  I agree `.calculator` is a more appropriate name but scripters might prefer the shorter version.  Oh well.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
So @jensj do you think society is ready for this revolutionizing change?

Right now it's the usually-invisible DeprecationWarning but we can change it to np.VisibleDeprecationWarning if we want people to actually see it and change things.

comments.author: jensj
comments.body: I think so, if we start with an invisible warning and a mention in the release notes for 3.20 and then a visible warning in 3.21.  Will pytest show these usually-invisible DeprecationWarnings?

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
@jensj pytest shows DeprecationWarnings by default.  Warning control can be done in pytest.ini.  Since the deprecated functions would by now be untested, I added unittests.  This is how to test deprecated functionality:

```
def test_del_calculator(atoms):
    atoms.calc = EMT()
    with pytest.deprecated_call():
        del atoms.calc
    assert atoms.calc is None
```

I silenced a mypy error because it can't handle decorated properties (for `del atoms.calc`).  Maybe some contributors will find it hard to work with this, since they just get errors from the pipeline that they don't necessarily know how to reproduce locally or otherwise circumvent (we also take a certain amount of flak (heh) for the flake8 errors).  But we'll have to see about that.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Presumably the latest changes are not so revolutionary so I'll just merge by now (if it passes).
